chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: The weird scene in the band: loners and non-talkers
summary: Sections barely spoke; Ray Nance and Al Killian were loners, Shorty Baker liked everyone, the trombones were close.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: What were the guys like in the band? How did you get along?

I got along with them beautiful. I'll get along with anybody. You know, Milt, just like I said before, if you live with love in your heart, it -- you know, people will know. I never had a minute's trouble with nobody.
Well, how was the band in general amongst one another?
Oh, that was a fun -- that was a weird scene.

So, Butter, what were you saying? It was a weird scene?

Yeah, it was a weird scene because sometimes the guys would sit on the bandstand and they wouldn't say nothing to each other, especially in the saxophone section. They didn't hang out together or anything. The trombones were always close. The trumpets were -- Ray always, he was a loner.
Yes. And Al Killian was a loner, by himself. Shorty used to hang out with anybody that was available that wanted to hang out. That's where Shorty Baker was at, you know?
